paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the empirical generalization errors on the RTE dataset for fine-tuned adapters across various hidden dimensions, titled "Errors (RTE)." The x-axis represents "Rank" on a logarithmic scale with tick labels at 4, 16, 64, and 256. The y-axis represents the error values on a linear scale, with tick labels at 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9. A single line is shown in black with a solid style, connecting green circular markers at each rank value. Error bars are displayed at each data point. At rank 4, the error is approximately 0.34; it decreases slightly to approximately 0.31 at rank 16, which represents the lowest point on the curve. The error then increases to approximately 0.40 at rank 64 and rises more steeply to approximately 0.61 at rank 256. The overall trend shows a slight initial decrease from rank 4 to rank 16, followed by a monotonic increase through ranks 64 and 256.
